tagline: Back roads north of Durham, past Stagville to a three-family crossroads.
intro: Off I-85 north of Durham the byway takes Old Oxford Road past the old plantation lands of Fairntosh and Stagville, then Bahama Road to the crossroads of Bahama and along the water of Lake Michie. From there it wanders north by Red Mountain Road and Moores Mill Road to US 501 near Rougemont, then out along Lowell Road through rolling farmland with horses in the pastures.
On US 501 it passes Quail Roost, organized as a hunt club by Durham men in 1875 and later one of the country's leading stables and dairy farms.

moments.title: Stagville
moments.text: At Horton Grove stand the only two-story slave quarters left in North Carolina, built in 1850 on a plantation complex where almost 900 people were enslaved in 1860.

moments.title: Bahama
moments.text: The crossroads answered to Balltown, Round Hill and Hunkadora until 1891, when it took the first letters of the Ball, Harris and Mangum families and became Bahama, said bah-HAY-ma.

moments.title: Lake Michie
moments.text: Bahama Road runs beside Durham's drinking water, a reservoir on the Flat River dammed between 1924 and 1926 that also supplied the city with hydroelectric power until 1960.

practical: The optional State Forest Road extension is gravel, with a rough bridge over the Eno River.
